subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
title: Listening and Speaking: Pronunciation and Vocabulary
overview: Clean surroundings give us clear things to talk about. In this sub-strand you will say the sounds /ʌ/ and /ɔː/ and the clusters br, sw, pr, cl and gr in words such as brush, water, broom, sweep, protect, clear and grass. You will speak at a steady speed, use gestures, and give a short speech about the environment.

lessons.title: Sounds, clusters and environment words
objectives: Say /ʌ/, /ɔː/ and the clusters br, sw, pr, cl and gr clearly.
Pick those words out of a short oral text.
Ask and answer yes or no questions about a clean environment.
lessons.intro: Say cup, then say water. The first vowel is short and open. The second is longer and made with rounded lips. Environment talk uses both, often beside clusters such as br in broom and gr in grass.
lessons.notes:
### The short sound /ʌ/
Open your mouth a little and keep the sound short. You hear it in cup, up, sun, cut, brush, rubbish, mud and dump. It is the vowel in the first part of the word rubbish. Do not stretch it into the long sound in food.

The word bush is different. A bush is a small woody plant, and its vowel is the short sound in put, not the sound in cup. Learn bush as a meaning word, and practise /ʌ/ with rubbish and brush.

### The long sound /ɔː/
Round your lips and hold the sound. You hear it in water, lawn, walk, saw, tall, all, floor and door. We walk across the lawn to fetch water. Do not cut the sound short, or water can be hard to recognise.

### Consonant clusters
Say the two consonants together, with no vowel between them.

- br: broom, brush, branch, bring
- sw: sweep, swim, swing
- pr: protect, proud, promise
- cl: clean, clear, class
- gr: grass, green, grow, ground

A broom sweeps. A brush scrubs. We protect rivers and trees. We clear a drain so that water can pass. Green grass grows when we care for the soil.

### Other useful words
The compound is the open ground around a home or school. A bin holds rubbish. A rubbish pit is a hole used for waste that can rot. A drain carries water away. A neighbourhood is the area around your home. Hills, rivers and trees are part of the environment. Cleanliness means keeping that environment clean. To conserve water means to use it carefully and not waste it.

### An oral text
Listen for the target sounds: 'Bring a broom and a brush. Sweep the rubbish off the lawn, then clear the drain so the water can run. Protect the young trees and let the grass grow.'

### Yes or no questions
A yes or no question can be answered with yes or no, often plus a short verb.

Do you sweep the compound? Yes, I do. / No, I do not.
Is the drain clear? Yes, it is. / No, it is not.
Can we protect the river? Yes, we can.

Speak the question as a whole, not one word at a time. Your voice usually rises a little at the end.

keyWords.meaning: the open ground around a house or school
a channel that carries water away
to use something carefully so that it is not wasted
the air, water, land, plants and animals around us

examples.problem: Sort these words: brush, water, sweep, grass, lawn, bring.
steps: Brush has /ʌ/ and br. Water and lawn have /ɔː/. Sweep has sw. Grass and bring have gr and br.
examples.answer: /ʌ/: brush. /ɔː/: water, lawn. br: brush, bring. sw: sweep. gr: grass.

examples.problem: Turn this statement into a yes or no question: The bin is full.
steps: Raise your voice slightly at the end.

activity.title: Hear it and answer
materials: Word cards for broom, sweep, protect, clear, grass, water, rubbish
steps: Listen to the oral text and repeat it without stopping after every word.
Hold up a card when you hear that word.
In pairs, ask three yes or no questions using the cards, and answer in short sentences.
Say one sentence of your own that includes a cluster, for example: Please bring a broom and sweep the path.

practice.question: Which words have /ʌ/: rubbish, water, cup, lawn, brush?
Write one word for each cluster: br, sw, pr, cl, gr.
practice.answer: Examples: broom, sweep, protect, clear, grass.

practice.question: Answer: Do you clear the drain when it is blocked?
practice.answer: Example: Yes, I do. or No, I do not.

practice.question: What does conserve water mean?
practice.answer: To use water carefully and not waste it.

summary: /ʌ/ is short, as in rubbish and brush. /ɔː/ is long, as in water and lawn.
Clusters br, sw, pr, cl and gr have no vowel between the consonants.
Yes or no questions can be answered with yes or no and a short verb.

lessons.title: Fluent speeches and messages without words
objectives: Speak a short text at the right speed and with expression.
Use gestures and facial expressions that match the message.
Explain why fluency helps a listener.
lessons.intro: A learner who says 'The... um... drain... is... um... blocked' makes the listener work too hard. The same fact, spoken in two smooth groups, is easier to act on: 'The drain is blocked. Please bring a broom.'
lessons.notes:
### What fluency means
Fluent speech is accurate, expressive and steady. Accurate means the sounds and words are right. Expressive means your voice shows feeling and importance. Steady means you move at a speed others can follow, with only short pauses. A little hesitation while you think is normal. Long gaps filled with 'um' break the message.

Group words that belong together. 'Clear the drain / beside the kitchen / before the rain.' Pause at the slashes, not after every word.

### The right speed
If you speak too fast, listeners miss whether you said bin or bush, or grass or glass. If you speak too slowly, they forget the beginning before you reach the end. Practise by repeating a short text after your teacher or a recording until you can say it once without a stumble.

Try this: 'Our class cares for the compound. We sweep the paths, clear the drains and water the young trees. A clean neighbourhood is safer for everyone.'

### Messages without words
You can support speech, or sometimes replace a word, with nonverbal cues.

- Point to the bin when you say bin.
- Hold up a broom when you ask for one.
- Shake your head at litter on the grass.
- A worried face shows that a blocked drain matters.
- A smile and a nod thank someone who has helped.

The cue must match the words. Smiling while you describe a dangerous, flooded drain confuses people. If you pass a message with no words at all, choose a gesture the group has agreed on, and check that they understood.

### Why fluency matters
A fluent speaker is easier to trust and easier to follow. In a clean-up, people need instructions they can hear the first time. Fluency also shows respect: you have prepared, so you do not waste the listeners' time. The same skill helps every time you present work in class.

keyWords.meaning: speech that is clear, expressive and steady, with little hesitation
the feeling and emphasis you put into your voice
an unwanted pause while you search for the next word
a message from the face, hands or body

examples.problem: Mark sensible pauses: Please sweep the path and empty the bin before lunch.
steps: Do not pause after every word.
examples.answer: Please sweep the path / and empty the bin / before lunch.

examples.problem: Which gesture matches the sentence 'Put the rubbish in the bin'?
steps: The important object is the bin.
Pointing to it supports the words.
examples.answer: Point to the bin, or mime dropping rubbish into it.

activity.title: A short speech on a clean place
materials: The model text in the notes
A broom, a bin or pictures of them
steps: Repeat the model text after the teacher until the group can say it with almost no hesitation.
In pairs, recite a short poem about the environment, keeping a steady rhythm and listening to each other's ideas with respect.
Prepare a short speech: name one dirty place, say what you will do, and say why it matters. Speak at a steady speed.
Add two nonverbal cues. The class says what those cues meant.

practice.question: What three things make speech fluent?
practice.answer: Accuracy, expression and the right speed, with little hesitation.

practice.question: Why is speaking too fast a problem?
practice.answer: Listeners may miss important words and not know what to do.

practice.question: Give one way to pass a message without words.
practice.answer: Example: Point to the bin, shake your head at litter, or mime using a broom.

practice.question: Why does fluency matter during a clean-up?
practice.answer: People can follow the instructions the first time and work safely together.

summary: Speak in phrases, at a speed listeners can follow.
Let your face and hands match the words.
Fluent instructions are easier and more respectful to follow.

quiz.question: Which word has the short sound /ʌ/?
quiz.explanation: Rubbish has the short vowel /ʌ/. Water, lawn and floor have /ɔː/.

quiz.question: Which word has the long sound /ɔː/?
quiz.explanation: Water has the long rounded sound /ɔː/.

quiz.question: Which word begins with the cluster sw?
quiz.explanation: Sweep begins with s and w together.

quiz.question: Which word begins with the cluster gr?
quiz.explanation: Grass begins with g and r together.

quiz.question: A drain is
options: a channel that carries water away
quiz.explanation: A drain carries water away from a place.

quiz.question: Which question can be answered with yes or no?
options: How do you make a broom?
quiz.explanation: Is the compound clean? can be answered yes or no.

quiz.question: Fluent speech is best described as
options: spoken one letter at a time
quiz.explanation: Fluency is clear, expressive speech at a followable speed.

quiz.question: Which gesture best matches 'Put the paper in the bin'?
options: Close your eyes and turn away
quiz.explanation: Pointing to the bin supports the instruction.

quiz.question: Why should you speak at the right speed?
quiz.answer: So listeners can hear each important word and remember the message.
quiz.explanation: Too fast hides words. Too slow breaks the message apart.

quiz.question: Why is fluency important when you give a speech?
quiz.answer: Listeners can follow you the first time, and you show respect for their time.
quiz.explanation: Fluent speech makes the message clear and considerate.
